Containers and APIs

Deploy and orchestrate Docker containers securely at scale.

1. Core Concept

  • ECS and EKS orchestrate containers. The underlying compute for those containers can be EC2 (you manage servers) or Fargate (serverless, AWS manages servers).

2. Key Services & Features

  • Amazon ECS:
    • AWS-native container orchestration.
    • Uses Task Definitions to define images, CPU/RAM, and networking.
    • Deeply integrated with IAM and ALB.
  • Amazon EKS:
    • Managed Kubernetes.
    • Standard for open-source container orchestration.
    • Higher operational overhead than ECS.
  • AWS Fargate:
    • Serverless compute engine for containers.
    • No EC2 instances to patch or manage.
    • Priced by CPU/RAM requested per task.
  • API Gateway:
    • Front door for APIs.
    • Handles rate limiting, throttling, and Cognito auth.
    • Connects directly to Lambda or container endpoints.

3. Architecture Rules

  • Assign IAM roles directly to ECS Tasks (Task Role), not to the underlying EC2 instance, for least privilege.
  • Store container images in Amazon ECR securely.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • A team wants to run Docker containers but refuses to manage or patch any EC2 instances.
    • Choose: ECS with Fargate launch type.
    • Why: Fargate handles all underlying infrastructure abstraction.
  • An API is receiving overwhelming traffic and needs rate-limiting and authorization before hitting backend containers.
    • Choose: API Gateway.
    • Why: It provides a managed tier for throttling, API keys, and auth offloading.

Q1 In Amazon EC2 Container Service, are other container types supported?
  • A Yes, EC2 Container Service supports any container service you need.
  • B Yes, EC2 Container Service also supports Microsoft container service.
  • C No, Docker is the only container platform supported by EC2 Container Service presently.
  • D Yes, EC2 Container Service supports Microsoft container service and Openstack.
Answer: C

Q4 A web-startup runs its very successful social news application on Amazon EC2 with an Elastic Load Balancer, an Auto-Scaling group of Java/Tomcat application-servers, and DynamoDB as data store. The main web-application best runs on m2 x large instances since it is highly memory- bound Each new deployment requires semi-automated creation and testing of a new AMI for the application servers which takes quite a while and is therefore only done once per week. Recently, a new chat feature has been implemented in nodejs and waits to be integrated in the architecture. First tests show that the new component is CPU bound Because the company has some experience with using Chef, they decided to streamline the deployment process and use AWS OpsWorks as an application life cycle tool to simplify management of the application and reduce the deployment cycles. What configuration in AWS OpsWorks is necessary to integrate the new chat module in the most cost-efficient and flexible way?
  • A Create one AWS OpsWorks stack, create one AWS OpsWorks layer, create one custom recipe.
  • B Create one AWS OpsWorks stack create two AWS OpsWorks layers create one custom recipe.
  • C Create two AWS OpsWorks stacks create two AWS OpsWorks layers create one custom recipe.
  • D Create two AWS OpsWorks stacks create two AWS OpsWorks layers create two custom recipe.
Answer: C

Q5 A healthcare organization is designing a workload on AWS. The design must run containers without provisioning or managing EC2 worker nodes with the least operational overhead. Which solution should be selected?
  • A Amazon Lightsail distributions
  • B EC2 Dedicated Hosts

  • D AWS Lambda layers
